findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting data integrity — idempotent Super Admin tenant creation
findings.issue: All definePlatformRoute POST handlers ignore Idempotency-Key. In the tenant-create UI, form.reset() occurs only after a received response. If POST /v1/platform/tenants commits but its response is lost, the form remains populated and a retry executes the handler again; provisionTenant treats the now-taken generated slug as a collision and deliberately creates a second tenant with a random suffix. No route or uniqueness guard ties the retry to the first operation.
findings.consequence: A routine lost-response retry can create two live properties, memberships, starter inventories and audit histories for one intended Super Admin action.
findings.correction: Add actor-scoped platform idempotency before executing platform mutators, hashing method, URL and parsed body and replaying the stored response. Give the Platform create form a submission-scoped fingerprint/key. Add a real-route lost-response/same-key test proving one tenant, owner membership, inventory and audit are created and the original 201 is replayed.

findings.criterion: 6 and cross-cutting data integrity — usable local-auth person creation
findings.issue: In local-auth mode, addPerson creates the account and returns its only temporary password, while replaySafe persists the successful response with temporaryPassword null. After a committed request whose response is lost, the same-key replay returns 201 without a credential and People reports users.invited even though no invitation exists. The apparent /forgot and /reset UI is Supabase-only; the local-auth branch has no reset/recovery API and the login screen exposes Forgot only when externalAuth is enabled.
findings.consequence: The member exists but neither the administrator nor the person received a usable credential, and retry/removal cannot provide one; the account is stranded behind a false invitation message.
findings.correction: Keep raw one-time passwords out of replay storage, but replace local creation with a recoverable setup/invitation flow or add an authenticated credential-recovery action and an explicit replay outcome. Add a lost-response API/UI test that follows the replay through successful first sign-in.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting data integrity — idempotent cross-property person creation
findings.issue: POST /v1/platform/tenants/:slug/members still runs through definePlatformRoute, which ignores the stable key People now supplies. After a committed response is lost, an exact retry reaches addPerson again and returns already_member; for a newly created local account the first temporary password was also lost. The rendered test mocks post and checks only that a key argument was passed, so it does not execute this server path.
findings.consequence: A required Super Admin cross-property write can report failure after success and leave the newly created person unable to sign in.
findings.correction: Apply tenant-scoped replay handling to the platform member endpoint and use the recoverable onboarding outcome above. Execute a same-key retry against the real endpoint and assert one account, membership and audit plus a usable sign-in/setup result.

findings.criterion: 1 — resident generates and shares a usable tamper-protected two-hour pass
findings.issue: The recorded green suite still does not execute the complete generated-pass chain in context. pass-e2e starts from a fabricated TOKEN, mounts GuestPass directly rather than entering /pass through AppProvider/App, and mocks lookup/redeem; separate API tests cover HMAC, verify_code and expiry but do not prove that the artifact produced by the resident Share control survives the real public bootstrap and gate validation as that same live pass.
findings.consequence: The required resident-generate → share → guest-open → scan → real gate-validation behavior remains unverified as an integrated user path.
findings.correction: Issue a live pass through the API, invoke the real resident Share control, open its fragment URL through /pass at a mobile viewport, decode the rendered QR, and perform real lookup/redeem. Assert exact token identity, the two-hour expiry, and HMAC plus verify_code tamper rejection in that joined run.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera plate scanning during check-in and check-out
findings.issue: The rendered tests replace LiveCamera with a button that emits an already-decoded plate. No recorded run executes getUserMedia, the shipped ONNX/model loader and decoder, a camera fixture or responsive browser behavior, and the existing browser camera story covers check-in only.
findings.consequence: Actual camera acquisition and plate decoding remain unverified in the shipped stack for both check-in and check-out.
findings.correction: Run and record the 390x844 fake-camera check-in story with the real model and .y4m fixture; add and run an equivalent checkout story. Assert the visible filled plate, checkout match request/result, browser/model/fixture versions and a clean console.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — complete Admin CRUD and Super Admin operations across properties
findings.issue: The rendered evidence completes CRUD only for a unit. Person is create-only; site/zone/slot are created but site and zone are not edited/retired, a slot is not edited, and deletion targets a pre-existing mocked slot. The Super Admin case performs only a mocked person POST in a second property. All APIs are mocked, and changing window.innerWidth in jsdom does not execute layout.
findings.consequence: Complete person/building/slot CRUD, representative all-entity operations in another property, persistence, authorization boundaries and mobile usability remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: Drive create/read/edit/delete or retire for person, site, unit and slot through the real routed UI and API in a narrow real browser. Enter a second property as Super Admin and perform representative writes for all entities there, asserting persisted results and regular-admin cross-property denial.

findings.issue: Ten review reports already existed and LOOP-SUMMARY identifies iteration 10 as the 10-iteration cap, but an eleventh implementation tick was still committed, fast-forwarded and pushed. The later time budget did not supersede the unchanged 10-iteration cap.
findings.consequence: The autonomous process exceeded the user's explicit maximum and published work after the loop was required to stop.
findings.correction: Stop the loop after this record; do not queue another implementation tick. Preserve the non-destructive published history and record the cap deviation for review rather than attempting a rollback or force operation.
